The experimental data from field, greenhouse, and laboratory studies presented by him showed that some isolates of R. solani seem to be less affected than others by the same test chemical or combination of chemicals. Other workers (EL SAID 1963, SHATLA and SINCLAIR 1963, and THOMAS 1962) demonstrated that adap- tation to certain fungicides takes place in Rhizoctonia solani. 2.5.2. Materials and methods Three isolates Sc. 8, Sc. 55 and Sc. 3 each representing one group were included in this study. Two antibiotics, terramycin hydrochloride and streptomycin sulfate each at 100 ppm were used. Desiccated ox-bile (= oxgall) was applied at concentrations of 1, 2.5, and 5 g/1, and boric acid at concentrations of 1 and 3 g/1 respectively. Four different media were included in these experiments viz: a. cherry agar, b. potato-dextrose agar (PDA), c. peptone agar, and d. Czapeck-Dox agar (Modified). The inoculum of R. solani was prepared in the same manner as previously reported. Five replicates were used for each treatment. The PETRI dishes were incubated at 24 °C and colony diameters were measured every 24 hours. 2.5.3. Results Table 3 shows the results of the experiments on linear growth of the three isolates. The data represent the average diameters recorded at the end of 3 days incubation, measurements showed very little variation between replicates. The growth was not affected by incorporation of terramycin or streptomycin in any of the four media. The growth rate was reduced considerably by incorporating 1 g/1 oxgall or 1 g/1 boric acid to the media with the exception of oxgall in PDA or Cz-Dox. Apparently in these cases the effect of oxgall has been neutra- lized by the medium. Boric acid in a concentration of 3 g/1 inhibited the growth of the three isolates completely. Ox bile powder is a whole bile matrix sourced from cattle gallbladders — not a single isolated bile salt, not a synthetic compound. Raw bile is collected at licensed processing facilities, then filtered, purified, concentrated, and low-temperature dehydrated into a standardized free-flowing powder. One gram of finished extract equals approximately 8 grams of fresh bile. The active composition includes primary bile acids (cholic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid), secondary bile acids (deoxycholic acid), taurine- and glycine-conjugated fractions, and phospholipids — all in naturally occurring ratios. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Solution A
